etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English forestallen (“to forestall, intercept, ambush, way-lay”), from forestalle (“a forestalling, interception”), from Old English foresteall (“intervention, hindrance of justice, ambush”), from fore- (“ahead of, before”) + steall (“position”), equivalent to fore- +‎ stall.
senses: (transitive) To prevent, delay or hinder something by taking precautionary or anticipatory measures; to avert.
(transitive) To preclude or bar from happening, render impossible.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: From Middle English forstal, from Old English foresteall (“an intervention, hindrance (of justice), ambush, assault, offence of waylaying on the highway, fine for such an offence, resistance, opposition”), equivalent to fore- +‎ stall.
senses: (obsolete or historical) An ambush; plot; an interception; waylaying; rescue.
Something situated or placed in front.
